subject: Cross platform Gaussian process kernel library

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Cross platform Gaussian process kernel library
parts:
James Hensman (Sheffield) and Nick Golding (Oxford) would like to talk with Stan people about cross platform Gaussian process kernel library
James writes:
> Okay, here's what we'd like:
> - A unified kernel library, with basic kernels built-in, and the
> ability to quickly prototype new kernels
> - symbolic differntiation of the kernel matrix construction (i.e.
> k[i,j] <- k(x[i], x[j])
> - ability to get at the functionality from other languages (not just
> run STAN from other languages, but use the kernels as part of other
> packages)

James wrote "symbolic differntiation" but he means "autodiff with exceptions for specific operations".

They already have kernel library in Python (GPy), so they have experience. They know that core team is busy with other things in Stan, but I think it it's good to talk with them as they probably could contribute significantly.

Is it ok if they join the Stan G+hangout today, so they could introduce themselves and say something what they could offer?

Aki

If we're going to add structured data types, then the
biggest hurdle is my time or finding someone else who
can modify the parser (or relieve me of some other duties
like writing doc, helping with grant proposals, and
answering user-facing mailing-list queries [the last of which I
know I should spend less time on the way Andrew knows he should
spend less time blogging!]).

- Bob
